title: A Tsunami Crosses the Open Ocean at Over 500 mph, as Fast as a Jet

scenes.text: A tsunami can cross the ocean as fast as a jet.
In deep water, it can travel over 500 miles an hour.
Out there, you'd barely notice it. It's only a few feet high at most.
But the wave is hundreds of miles long, so a huge amount of water is moving.
Near the coast, it slows to about 20 to 30 miles an hour, like a car. The water piles up.
A jet at sea. A car at the coast.

description:
In deep ocean, a tsunami can travel at more than 500 miles an hour, about the speed of a jet.
In open water it is barely noticeable, but its wavelength can stretch hundreds of miles. Near the coast it slows to 20 to 30 miles an hour and the water piles up.
Did you know tsunamis move that fast? Comment below.
first_comment: In deep water you wouldn't even notice it. That's what makes tsunami warnings so important. What would you do with 30 minutes of warning?
